figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Model of malleicyprol biosynthesis. A) Two strategies are used by nonribosomal peptide synthetases for selecting and incorporating α-
hydroxy acids into depsipeptides. B) R-Trigonic acid biosynthesis in B. thailandensis and proposed model of malleicyprol assembly on BurF. The bur
gene cluster of Burkholderia thailandensis encodes enzymes for the biosynthesis of R-trigonic acid (light blue). The biosynthesis is initiated by
converting L-methionine to 2R,3R-gonydiol by the actions of six enzymes. Subsequently, the cyclopropanol moiety is assembled by BurG. On BurF,
the thiolation domain of module 3 is proposed for loading of the α-hydroxy acid 5, but the required domains to load 5 onto the thiolation domain
with known strategies are absent in this module. See Figure S1 for a detailed Scheme of the biosynthetic pathway. M: module; ACP: acyl carrier
protein; KS: ketosynthase; DH: dehydratase; KR: ketoreductase; MT: methyltransferase; AT: acyltransferase; C: condensation domain; T: thiolation
domain; Red: reductase.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. BurJ activates trigonic acid and binds it onto its T domain. A)
Structural model of BurJ highlighting the two-domain architecture. B)
Trigonic acid quantification in PburΔburJ (error bars represent the
mean of three replicatesSD). C) BurJ activates trigonic acid and
forms an enzyme-bound intermediate. D) Phosphate determination
(error bars represent the mean of three replicatesSD). n. d. not
detected; ACP: acyl carrier protein; A domain: adenylation domain;
Pant: pantetheine.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. BurH transfers trigonic acid onto BurF. A) Standard FkbH-like
proteins use 1,3-BPG as a substrate and bind it onto a conserved
cysteine residue. The bound intermediate is then dephosphorylated by
a phosphatase domain which usually contains conserved aspartate
residues. B) Genetic inactivation of burH prevents the formation of
malleicyprol. Genetic complementation restores malleicyprol biosyn-
thesis. C) Trigonic acid quantification in PburΔburH (error bars
represent the mean of three replicatesSD). D) Phylogenetic analysis
and modeling of BurH. E) Trigonic acid is transferred onto BurH. A
BurH C345 mutant does not show binding of trigonic acid. F) Trigonic
acid is transferred onto BurF from BurJ mediated by BurH. n. d.: not
detected.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. A multienzymatic gateway directs trigonic acid onto BurF and
genome mining for noncanonical FkbH-like proteins. A) BurJ activates
the α-hydroxy acid and generates enzyme-bound trigonic acid. BurH
acts as mediator and transfers trigonic acid onto BurF. The mutated
phosphatase domain of BurH is indicated as P*. B) Sequence similarity
network of BurH homologs. The homologs belonging to the group
encoding a trans-ACP were color-coded to represent other adjacent
biosynthetic genes. C) Biosynthetic gene clusters that encode a BurH
homolog with modified phosphatase domain adjacent to a BurJ
homolog.
